description: Two delay lines that can be looped and reversed, their times set from one shared ping and stepped in whole multiples of it

params.text: Sets that channel's delay as a multiple of the pinged time, in seventeen steps from once up to sixteen times
Shifts that channel's whole range of times: 1/8TH divides the pinged time by eight, = leaves it alone, and +16 multiplies it by sixteen
Tap it twice to set the time both channels work from
Sets how much of that channel's delayed signal is fed back in, up to 110%, so past full the loop grows rather than dies away
Reverses the direction that channel's delay is read in
Holds what is in that channel's delay line, so it loops round and nothing new is written in
Sets how much of the input is written into that channel's delay line
Crossfades that channel's output between the dry input and the delayed signal

inputs.text: A trigger sets the time both channels work from; two edges above 0.1V give the period
That channel's input, up to 10V; with nothing in IN B, channel B takes whatever is in IN A
The return of that channel's send and return loop: whatever is patched here is what goes into the delay line
A trigger or a gate above 0.1V reverses that channel, as chosen on the menu
A trigger or a gate above 0.1V holds that channel's loop, as chosen on the menu
Moves that channel's delay time; the voltage is read upside down, so -5V lengthens it and +5V shortens it
Adds to that channel's FEEDBACK knob, 0V to 5V covering the whole range
Adds to that channel's DELAY FEED knob, 0V to 5V covering the whole range

outputs.text: A 5V trigger at the start of each loop of that channel's delay
A 5V clock at the pinged time, taken from channel B
That channel's output; with nothing patched into OUT B, OUT A carries both channels summed and halved
That channel's send: the signal on its way into the delay line, for an effect to be patched between send and return

notes: The two channels share one ping. Tapping the button or pinging the jack sets the time both work from, and each channel's TIME knob and switch then take their own multiple of it.
The send and return jacks form a loop around each delay line: patch an effect from SEND into RETURN and it is heard inside the feedback path.
menu: Soft Clip A — when on, channel A's delay line compresses as it reaches full scale rather than clipping flat
Soft Clip B — when on, channel B's delay line compresses as it reaches full scale rather than clipping flat
AutoMute A — when on, channel A's input is faded down while it stays quiet and faded back up when it returns
AutoMute B — when on, channel B's input is faded down while it stays quiet and faded back up when it returns
Ping Method: Avg 4, Avg 2, 1:1, IgnoreJitter, Ignore%Change — sets how a new ping time is taken: averaged over four pings or two, taken as it comes, or refused if it strays too far
Hold A: Trig, Gate — sets whether channel A's HOLD jack toggles the hold or holds it only while the jack is high
Hold B: Trig, Gate — sets whether channel B's HOLD jack toggles the hold or holds it only while the jack is high
Rev. A: Trig, Gate — sets whether channel A's REVERSE jack toggles the direction or reverses only while the jack is high
Rev. B: Trig, Gate — sets whether channel B's REVERSE jack toggles the direction or reverses only while the jack is high
DelayFeed A Taper: Log, Lin — sets the law of channel A's DELAY FEED knob
DelayFeed B Taper: Log, Lin — sets the law of channel B's DELAY FEED knob
Time A Auto-UnQ: Off, On — when on, a voltage at channel A's TIME jack moves the delay smoothly instead of snapping to the knob's steps
Time B Auto-UnQ: Off, On — when on, a voltage at channel B's TIME jack moves the delay smoothly instead of snapping to the knob's steps
Stereo Mode A: Off, On — when on, channel A's buffer holds a stereo pair, its IN and RETURN jacks becoming the two sides
Stereo Mode B: Off, On — when on, channel B's buffer holds a stereo pair, its IN and RETURN jacks becoming the two sides
Crossfade A: 1ms, 2ms, 4ms, 8ms, 25ms, 100ms, 250ms — sets how long channel A's read head takes to fade across when the delay time changes
Crossfade B: 1ms, 2ms, 4ms, 8ms, 25ms, 100ms, 250ms — sets how long channel B's read head takes to fade across when the delay time changes
